# Recommendation policy v1.1 (docs/specification/recommendation_policy.md), as data.
# Frozen 2026-11-12. Do not edit after final test results have been viewed (development rule 12).
version: "1.1"
frozen: "2026-11-12"
default_tier_threshold: T2

references:
  FIPS203: "NIST FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard (ML-KEM), Aug 2024"
  FIPS204: "NIST FIPS 204, Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard (ML-DSA), Aug 2024"
  FIPS205: "NIST FIPS 205, Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard (SLH-DSA), Aug 2024"
  SP800-227: "NIST SP 800-227, Recommendations for Key-Encapsulation Mechanisms, Sep 2025"
  IR8547: "NIST IR 8547, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, final, Oct 2026"

classes:
  SIG:
    family: SIG
    target: "ML-DSA (FIPS 204); SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) where its size/speed trade-offs are acceptable"
    parameter_set: "ML-DSA-65 (category 3) by default; ML-DSA-44 only with an RBG of >= 192-bit strength if category 2 is required; ML-DSA-87 for category 5"
    references: [FIPS204, FIPS205, IR8547]
  KEM:
    family: KEM
    target: "ML-KEM-based key-establishment redesign (FIPS 203, SP 800-227); PQ/T hybrid with the existing scheme through an approved combiner is an acceptable transitional design"
    parameter_set: "ML-KEM-768 (NIST IR 8547 default recommendation)"
    references: [FIPS203, SP800-227, IR8547]
  KEM_DEM:
    family: KEM
    target: "Redesign as KEM + KDF + AEAD (KEM/DEM, SP 800-227 Secs. 2.1, 5.2); not a drop-in replacement for encrypt/decrypt"
    parameter_set: "ML-KEM-768 (NIST IR 8547 default recommendation) with an approved KDF and AEAD"
    references: [FIPS203, SP800-227, IR8547]
  INVENTORY:
    family: NONE
    target: "No migration target at this site; inventory the key material and determine its downstream role"
    references: []
  PROTOCOL_REVIEW:
    family: NONE
    target: "Protocol/library migration review (enable PQC or hybrid options of the protocol library)"
    references: [IR8547]
  NO_ACTION_HYBRID:
    family: NONE
    target: "No migration of this component now: it is the traditional half of a PQ/T hybrid with an approved PQ algorithm; plan a PQC-only follow-up"
    references: [SP800-227, IR8547]
  ABSTAIN:
    family: NONE
    target: "No recommendation: evidence is insufficient"
    references: []

roles:
  SIGN: SIG
  VERIFY: SIG
  KEY_ESTABLISHMENT: KEM
  PK_ENCRYPT: KEM_DEM
  PK_DECRYPT: KEM_DEM
  KEY_MATERIAL_ONLY: INVENTORY
  PROTOCOL_CONFIG: PROTOCOL_REVIEW
  UNKNOWN: ABSTAIN

# Approved PQ component per role (policy Sec. 2, NO_ACTION_HYBRID: "whose PQ component is a NIST-approved
# scheme (ML-KEM; ML-DSA/SLH-DSA for signatures)"). The PQ API must be of the matching family and be used
# in the same class or function as the site. Encoding fix 2026-11-14 (independent review finding 1): an
# earlier encoding accepted any PQ family for any role. Policy text and version are unchanged.
approved_hybrid_prefixes:
  KEY_ESTABLISHMENT:
    - "cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.mlkem."
  SIGN:
    - "cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.mldsa."
  VERIFY:
    - "cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.mldsa."

templates:
  SIGN: >-
    {alg} signing is deprecated after 2030 and disallowed after 2035 (NIST IR 8547 Table 2). Migrate signing
    to ML-DSA (FIPS 204); dual/hybrid signatures are a transitional option; verifiers and certificate chains
    must be able to accept ML-DSA before signers switch.
  SIGN_DSA: >-
    DSA is no longer specified in FIPS 186-5 and is not listed in NIST IR 8547 Table 2; migrate to ML-DSA (FIPS 204).
  VERIFY: >-
    Add ML-DSA (FIPS 204) verification so that migrated signers can be accepted. NIST IR 8547 defines 'legacy use'
    as processing already-protected data such as verifying an existing signature; whether {alg} verification of
    already-issued signatures keeps that status after 2035 is set by SP 800-131A (to be revised). Retain legacy
    verification only for already-issued signatures; do not accept new {alg} signatures after the transition.
  KEY_ESTABLISHMENT: >-
    {alg} key establishment is deprecated after 2030 and disallowed after 2035 (NIST IR 8547 Table 4) and is exposed
    to harvest-now-decrypt-later. Redesign around ML-KEM (FIPS 203; ML-KEM-768 recommended by NIST IR 8547) per
    SP 800-227; a PQ/T hybrid with the existing scheme via an approved combiner (SP 800-227 Sec. 4.6) is an acceptable
    transitional design. ML-KEM uses encapsulate/decapsulate, not a symmetric exchange(peer) call.
  PK_ENCRYPT: >-
    RSA public-key encryption / key transport (PKCS#1 v1.5, OAEP) has no drop-in PQC replacement. Redesign as
    KEM + KDF + AEAD (SP 800-227 Secs. 2.1, 5.2): the sender encapsulates to the recipient's authenticated ML-KEM key,
    derives the content key from the shared secret (FIPS 203 Sec. 3.3), and encrypts with an AEAD. The existing
    encrypt(data) call shape cannot be preserved.
  PK_DECRYPT: >-
    RSA public-key decryption / key unwrapping has no drop-in PQC replacement. Redesign as KEM + KDF + AEAD
    (SP 800-227 Secs. 2.1, 5.2), decapsulation side: decapsulate with the ML-KEM decapsulation key, derive the content
    key from the shared secret (FIPS 203 Sec. 3.3), and decrypt with an AEAD. The existing decrypt(ciphertext) call
    shape cannot be preserved.
  KEY_MATERIAL_ONLY: >-
    {alg} key material with no consumer found in the analysed scope. No target is recommended; determine the
    downstream role first.
  PROTOCOL_CONFIG: >-
    Protocol configuration site. Migrate by enabling the library's PQC/hybrid options; do not replace primitives here.
  HYBRID: >-
    Traditional component of a PQ/T hybrid with an approved PQ algorithm; no migration of this component is required
    now; hybrids are transitional (NIST IR 8547) - plan a PQC-only follow-up; review the combiner per SP 800-227 Sec. 4.6.
  ABSTAIN_UNKNOWN: >-
    Role cannot be determined: {missing}. Possible roles: {possible}. No single target is justified.
  ABSTAIN_TIER: >-
    Evidence tier {tier} is below the policy threshold {threshold}: {missing}. Inferred role (not acted on): {role}.

=== BEGIN DOCUMENT: docs/benchmark/ai_review_prompt_v1.md (sha256 cdd20fa67c700ea9a69ef98851f7fc93e4995b847c01ca18324c1d3702eafd76) ===
You are reviewing Python call sites that use public-key cryptography (RSA, elliptic-curve, X25519/X448, Ed25519/Ed448)
through the libraries pyca/cryptography or PyCryptodome. For each candidate below, decide its labels by following the
decision procedure and the evidence rules that follow this introduction, using ONLY the code shown in that
candidate's packet. Do not assume anything about code that is not shown.

For each candidate, output exactly one JSON object on its own line, with these keys:

{"candidate_id": "<as given>", "status": "ok" or "insufficient_context",
 "eligible": true or false, "gt_role": "<SIGN|VERIFY|KEY_ESTABLISHMENT|PK_ENCRYPT|PK_DECRYPT|KEY_MATERIAL_ONLY|PROTOCOL_CONFIG|UNKNOWN|NONE>",
 "assessability": "<DETERMINATE|INDETERMINATE>", "possible_roles": [<roles, required when gt_role is UNKNOWN>],
 "hybrid_component": true or false, "obvious_from_name": true or false,
 "evidence_needed": "<none|argument-resolution|downstream-usage|protocol-context|runtime-value>",
 "key_provenance": "<generated|loaded-PEM|loaded-DER|loaded-SSH|loaded-JWK|loaded-certificate|constructed-from-parsed-blob|parameter|attribute|env-or-KMS|unknown|n/a>",
 "ambiguity": "<none|guide_unclear|context_insufficient>",
 "evidence_lines": ["<file>:<line>", ...], "rationale": "<one or two sentences>"}

Use "status": "insufficient_context" when the packet does not contain enough code to decide; still fill every field
you can decide and explain what is missing in the rationale. Use JSON booleans (true/false), not strings. Output the
JSON lines only, one per candidate, in the order given.

The decision procedure and the evidence rules follow.

=== BEGIN DOCUMENT: pqscan/bench/packets.py (sha256 636b4b8f68fc315dc5d2c504b566452c1a89f477e0567116a6bdb89a6f493925) ===
"""Annotation packets for the blind AI-assisted review (protocol v1.0.4 Sec. 3; guide v1.1 Sec. 5-6; V8, V16;
R4-19 item 5).

Packet rule `packet-v1` (fixed; its hash is recorded at F1). For candidate (file, line) of a repository checkout at
its pinned commit, the packet contains, from that one file only:
  1. a header: candidate ID, file path (relative), line;
  2. every top-level import statement of the file;
  3. the context: the smallest enclosing class if it has at most CLASS_MAX_LINES lines, otherwise the smallest
     enclosing function; at module level, WINDOW lines either side of the candidate;
  4. up to MAX_CALLERS other functions in the same file that call the enclosing function by name (Step D: the direct
     caller, one level).
Every source line is prefixed with its line number; the candidate line is marked ">>". The source code is never
executed or imported; it is read as text and parsed with `ast`. Nothing outside the file is included, so labels that
need more context are recorded by the owner as `context_used = extended`.

Forbidden content: the packet template itself never contains tool names, the project's name, hypotheses or results
(FORBIDDEN). Source code is copied verbatim; if the scanned code itself contains a forbidden token, the packet is
still built and the token is reported in `warnings` for the owner to review, never silently edited.

Packet-first subset: a candidate is labelled packet-first iff u < rate(phase), where u is a uniform value from
SHA-256("20261113:packet:<phase>|<candidate_id>") and rate(phase) = max(0.10, 60 / planned issued candidates of the
phase). The planned counts are the workload estimates of R3-03 (DV about 468, T about 630), so the expected subset
is at least 60 (target >= 50; the realised count is reported, and a shortfall cannot be topped up later because
packet-first labels must precede the primary label).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import hashlib
import re
from pathlib import Path

RULE = "packet-v1"
CLASS_MAX_LINES, WINDOW, MAX_CALLERS = 400, 40, 3
# tool names, the project's name and the study's hypotheses/arms; matched case-insensitively on word boundaries
FORBIDDEN = ("pqscan", "pqcheck", "pqc-audit", "pqc_audit", "postquant", "qsafe", "pqblocks", "cbomkit",
             "quantum-safe auditor", "semgrep", "pypqc", "rolebench", "post-quantum crypto scanner", "provenance-aware",
             "method+args", "h2a", "h2b")
_FORBIDDEN_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![a-z0-9_])(" + "|".join(re.escape(t) for t in FORBIDDEN) + r")(?![a-z0-9_])")
PACKET_SEED = 20261113
PLANNED_CANDIDATES = {"DV": 468, "T": 630}


def _forbidden_in(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return sorted({m.group(1) for m in _FORBIDDEN_RE.finditer(text.lower())})


def _span(node: ast.AST) -> tuple[int, int]:
    start = min([node.lineno] + [d.lineno for d in getattr(node, "decorator_list", [])])
    return start, node.end_lineno


def _enclosing(tree: ast.AST, line: int):
    cls = fn = None
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.ClassDef, ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
            a, b = _span(node)
            if a <= line <= b:
                if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
                    if cls is None or _span(node)[0] >= _span(cls)[0]:
                        cls = node
                elif fn is None or _span(node)[0] >= _span(fn)[0]:
                    fn = node
    return cls, fn


def _callers(tree: ast.AST, name: str, exclude: tuple[int, int]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    out = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and _span(node) != exclude:
            for sub in ast.walk(node):
                if isinstance(sub, ast.Call):
                    f = sub.func
                    callee = f.id if isinstance(f, ast.Name) else f.attr if isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) else None
                    if callee == name:
                        out.append(_span(node))
                        break
    return sorted(set(out))[:MAX_CALLERS]


def build_packet(repo_root: Path, file: str, line: int, candidate_id: str) -> dict:
    text = (Path(repo_root) / file).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    lines = text.splitlines()
    if not 1 <= line <= len(lines):
        raise ValueError(f"{file}:{line} is outside the file ({len(lines)} lines)")
    header = f"Candidate: {candidate_id}\nFile: {file}\nLine: {line}\n"
    bad = _forbidden_in(header)
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"packet header would contain forbidden content: {bad}")
    sections: list[tuple[str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
    notes = []
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(text)
    except (SyntaxError, ValueError):
        tree = None
        notes.append("the file does not parse; a line window is shown")
    if tree is not None:
        imports = [_span(n) for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom))]
        if imports:
            sections.append(("Imports", imports))
        cls, fn = _enclosing(tree, line)
        if cls is not None and _span(cls)[1] - _span(cls)[0] + 1 <= CLASS_MAX_LINES:
            ctx = _span(cls)
            sections.append(("Enclosing class", [ctx]))
        elif fn is not None:
            ctx = _span(fn)
            sections.append(("Enclosing function", [ctx]))
        else:
            ctx = (max(1, line - WINDOW), min(len(lines), line + WINDOW))
            sections.append(("Module context", [ctx]))
        if fn is not None:
            calls = [s for s in _callers(tree, fn.name, _span(fn)) if not (ctx[0] <= s[0] and s[1] <= ctx[1])]
            if calls:
                sections.append((f"Callers of {fn.name} in this file", calls))
    else:
        sections.append(("Line window", [(max(1, line - WINDOW), min(len(lines), line + WINDOW))]))
    width = len(str(len(lines)))
    body = [header]
    for title, spans in sections:
        body.append(f"--- {title} ---")
        for a, b in spans:
            for i in range(a, b + 1):
                mark = ">>" if i == line else "  "
                body.append(f"{mark} {i:>{width}} | {lines[i - 1]}")
            body.append("")
    if notes:
        body.append("Note: " + "; ".join(notes))
    packet_text = "\n".join(body).rstrip() + "\n"
    return {"rule": RULE, "candidate_id": candidate_id, "file": file, "line": line, "text": packet_text,
            "sha256": hashlib.sha256(packet_text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
            "warnings": [f"source contains forbidden token(s) {w}" for w in [_forbidden_in(text)] if w]}


def packet_first_rate(phase: str) -> float:
    if phase not in PLANNED_CANDIDATES:
        raise ValueError(f"packet-first applies to phases {sorted(PLANNED_CANDIDATES)}, not {phase!r}")
    return max(0.10, 60 / PLANNED_CANDIDATES[phase])


def packet_first(candidate_id: str, phase: str) -> bool:
    h = hashlib.sha256(f"{PACKET_SEED}:packet:{phase}|{candidate_id}".encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    return int(h[:16], 16) / 2**64 < packet_first_rate(phase)


def is_candidate_id(s: str) -> bool:
    return bool(re.fullmatch(r"[CA]-[0-9a-f]{12}", s))
=== END DOCUMENT: pqscan/bench/packets.py ===


END OF PACKET (PART 5 OF 5). Now produce the review in the OUTPUT FORMAT given in PART 1.
